title: Constraints
raw_text:
9/29/26, 9:47 AM
1. You define a time-of-use interface and select it for execution in EDM.

You use time-of-use formulas with a formula class. SAP provides formula classes for aggregation and determination of peak
demand values. You can also define your own formula classes.

2. You import the profile values in the SAP system - for example, using BAP! BAPI_ISUPROFILE IMPORT.

3. You execute billing as normal.

Constraints

Billing in combination with period-end billing, backbilling, or billing in advance is only possible with restrictions. Operands that
receive values from the time-of-use interface can only be used in rate steps that belong to the periodic billing period.

Time-of-Use Interface

Use

You can use the time-of-use interface to aggregate the profiles for billing. The interface contains the periods (for example, a
weekday in summer 08:00 17:59) and time-of-use formulas (for example, consumption above limit value), which are used to
process the profile values transfer them to the rate for billing. The following figure uses an example to illustrate this:

Example of a Time-of-Use Interface

Interval Length

The interval length for the time-of-use interface must be the same as the interval length for the profile.

Periods and Formulas

In the example above the year is divided into summer and winter. In summer you can choose from weekdays, weekends, public
holidays, and exception days (such as the football world cup final day). Whilst for weekdays, consumption and demand are
calculated using other formulas based on the time of day, only consumption is calculated for weekends.

You can define how the year can be divided into sections in Customizing. You can also map the year as a season group, or as a
group with the season types summer, winter, and transition. For each season, you determine in the time-of-use interface, the type
